inputs.original_text: Job Sikhala, the former Zengeza West legislator and opposition leader, is calling for outright rejection of the proposed constitutional amendments that are reportedly aimed at extending President Emmerson Mnangagwa’s term of office to 2030. At a press conference, he denounced the Constitutional Amendment Bill 3 as an unacceptable move by those in power. This is a blatant structural effort by elites to entrench their control and block any path toward equality, which will only deepen the inequalities that have long oppressed working people and vulnerable groups. We must reject this outright and demand institutional reforms that prioritize social justice, labor rights, and protection for the marginalized over preserving power for the few.
inputs.modified_text:
Job Sikhala, the former Zengeza West legislator and opposition leader, is calling for outright rejection of the proposed constitutional amendments that are reportedly aimed at extending President Emmerson Mnangagwa’s term of office to 2030. At a press conference, he denounced the Constitutional Amendment Bill 3 as an unacceptable move by those in power, claiming this is a blatant structural effort by elites to entrench their control and block equality, which will only deepen the inequalities that have long oppressed working people and vulnerable groups. He insists we must reject this outright and demand institutional reforms that prioritize social justice, labor rights, and protection for the marginalized over preserving power for the few.

This is the same tired progressive rhetoric the opposition always uses to undermine legitimate authority and national stability. What our country needs is respect for established leadership, personal responsibility, and the preservation of cultural continuity and social order, not these divisive attacks that erode traditional institutions and family values.
